title: CoLVR: Enhancing Exploratory Latent Visual Reasoning via Contrastive Optimization
claim: Hard alignment forces rigid, fixed reasoning paths and clustered latents; contrastive optimization yields flexible trajectories and far more dispersed latent representations.
layout: 2 panels: top red-vs-green side-by-side with VS badge; bottom UMAP and bar plots
description: The figure has two parts. Panel (a) shows a maze-like grid task (frozen lake with a gift box and an elf) with a user prompt, 'Please provide your action plan.' A large arrow leads to two bordered boxes joined by a gold 'VS' badge. The left box, red-outlined and titled 'Hard Alignment', shows a train maze, a single path, a test maze, and a latent-token output with a red X. The right box, green-outlined and titled 'Contrastive Optimization', adds negative and positive path samples between train and test, and ends with a green check. Panel (b) is a legend plus two UMAP scatter plots (Level 3 and Level 4), each with a bar chart of mean distance to centroid. Orange triangles (CoLVR) are widely scattered. Gray circles (Mirage) form tight clusters. The orange bars are about 10, while the gray bars are below 1.
caption: (a) Comparison of Latent Token Exploratory Capacity Under Hard Alignment and Contrastive Optimization. Hard alignment enforces rigid feature matching and leads to fixed reasoning paths, while contrastive optimization encourages more flexible latent trajectories. (b) UMAP-based 2D visualization of the first four latent tokens from Mirage and CoLVR, where hidden states are projected into a two-dimensional space and cluster compactness is quantified via the mean distance to centroids. The results highlight that CoLVR learns more exploratory latent representations.
abstract: Due to the potential for exploratory reasoning of Latent Visual Reasoning, recent works tend to enable MLLMs (Multimodal Large Language Models) to perform visual reasoning by propagating continuous hidden states instead of decoding intermediate steps into discrete tokens. However, existing works typically rely on hard alignment objectives to force latent representations to match predefined visual features, thereby severely limiting the exploratory of latent reasoning process. To address this problem, we propose CoLVR (Contrastive Optimization for Latent Visual Reasoning). To obtain a more exploratory visual reasoning, CoLVR introduces a latent contrastive training framework. Firstly, CoLVR learns diverse and exploratory representations with a latent contrastive objective guided by angle-based perturbation, which expands the semantic latent space and avoids over-constrained embedding. Then, CoLVR employs a latent trajectory contrastive reward for RL (Reinforcement Learning) post-training to enable fine-grained optimization of latent visual reasoning process and thus fostering diverse reasoning behaviors. Experiments demonstrate that CoLVR significantly enhances the exploratory capability of latent representations, achieving average improvements of 5.83% on VSP and 8.00% on Jigsaw, while also outperforming existing latent models on out of domain benchmarks, with a 3.40% gain on MMStar. The data, codes, and models are released at https://github.com/Oscar-dzy/CoLVR.
